domain_assessment.domain: Nuclear power plant operations during post-refueling reactor power ascension
domain_assessment.objective: Safely manage a scheduled reactor power ascension while detecting, evaluating, and escalating developing equipment-performance concerns.
domain_assessment.incident_type: A slowly worsening feedwater-pump vibration trend was initially monitored during ascension and subsequently required formal close monitoring under a technical-specification statement.

decision_points.summary: At the initial feedwater-pump pressure oscillation and vibration increase, the supervisor logs the condition and increases the monitoring interval rather than immediately involving the system engineer.
evidence_before: Pump 1B discharge pressure showed a slow upward oscillation.
The vibration monitor was increasing but remained within the normal band.
evidence_after: No immediate operability call or system-engineer escalation occurred.
goals_constraints: Avoid unnecessary escalation for a weak early signal.
Maintain appropriate surveillance during a routine ascension.
Preserve engineering attention for conditions requiring technical assessment.
alternatives: Log and increase monitoring, escalating only if the trend persists.
decision_points.decision_basis: The condition was within the normal band, had no alarm, and lacked sufficient trend history to establish a meaningful deviation.
decision_points.time_pressure: Low to moderate; the ascension was underway but no immediate deadline governed this choice.
decision_points.uncertainty: Whether the early oscillation represented normal variation or an emerging equipment issue.

decision_points.summary: After a brief steam-generator narrow-range level blip during rod withdrawal, the supervisor calls the on-call reactor engineer rather than relying exclusively on his own interpretation.
evidence_before: Steam generator B experienced a brief level blip during rod withdrawal.
Automatic control corrected the level within seconds.
A separate pump-vibration item was already being tracked.
evidence_after: The on-call reactor engineer was consulted.
The engineer characterized the event as consistent with known control response at that power level.
goals_constraints: Verify a control-system explanation rather than assume it.
Maintain safe ascension operations while two developing observations are present.
Obtain domain-specific confirmation without treating the event as an emergency.
alternatives: Rely on the supervisor's own assessment.
Call the reactor engineer for confirmation.
Pause the ascension pending a more formal review.
decision_points.decision_basis: The automatic response removed urgency, but the coexistence of two developing items warranted an independent technical view.
decision_points.time_pressure: Moderate; the evolution continued, but the event had stabilized.
decision_points.uncertainty: Whether the transient was a benign expected control response or evidence of a broader developing issue.

decision_points.summary: When pump vibration reaches the upper third of its normal band, the supervisor chooses the familiar continue-and-monitor response and does not retrieve accessible historical comparative trend data or hold the ascension for documented review.
evidence_before: Pump vibration had continued rising and was now in the upper third of the normal band.
The parameter had not reached an alarm or technical-specification limit.
Historical vibration comparisons were accessible on the plant computer.
The supervisor was simultaneously preparing materials for a surveillance-test pre-brief due in about 45 minutes and managing the ascension schedule.
evidence_after: The crew continued toward the next hold point under standard monitoring.
The historical comparison was not performed until after the pre-brief.
The later comparison showed a rate of rise unlike prior benign cases.
The pump subsequently entered formal close monitoring.
goals_constraints: Maintain the scheduled ascension toward the next hold point.
Complete the surveillance-test pre-brief preparation on time.
Manage an unresolved but non-alarming equipment trend.
Avoid an unnecessary hold or escalation while preserving operational safety.
alternatives: Retrieve and compare historical vibration-rate data before continuing.
Hold the ascension pending engineering review.
Continue with the standard monitor-and-continue checklist response.
Delegate or request assistance with the comparative review.
decision_points.decision_basis: The supervisor relied on prior successful use of the familiar checklist response and judged a fuller comparison unnecessary in the available attention window.
decision_points.time_pressure: Moderate and divided: a time-boxed pre-brief and ascension schedule competed for attention, although no imminent turnover handoff was present.
decision_points.uncertainty: Whether the ongoing rise was comparable to previously benign trends or had a materially different rate-of-rise profile.

decision_points.summary: During the surveillance-test pre-brief, the supervisor mentions the vibration trend only briefly and defers fuller discussion until after the meeting.
evidence_before: The test coordinator raised an unrelated procedural question that touched on the vibration item.
The trend had already been mentally framed as a monitor-and-continue item.
The pre-brief was not intended as the primary forum for evaluating the pump trend.
evidence_after: The supervisor mentioned the trend in passing without detail.
A fuller historical review was deferred until the pre-brief ended.
The supervisor later completed the comparison because the item had continued to nag at him.
goals_constraints: Keep the pre-brief focused on its scheduled purpose.
Maintain awareness of the vibration issue.
Avoid disrupting an unrelated procedural meeting.
alternatives: Provide a fuller description and request immediate discussion.
Briefly note the condition and return to the meeting agenda.
Pause or defer the pre-brief to conduct a trend review.
decision_points.decision_basis: The supervisor treated the item as already provisionally understood and intended to revisit it after the competing task.
decision_points.time_pressure: Moderate; the scheduled pre-brief was underway, but there was no turnover or handoff deadline.
decision_points.uncertainty: Whether the vibration trend warranted immediate broader communication despite remaining within normal operating limits.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “The continue-and-monitor approach is what we've used for trends like this before, and it's worked, so that's the direction I went. Pulling the historical vibration comparison off the plant computer was something I could've done — the data was right there — but between the pre-brief materials and the schedule, it didn't feel necessary in that window.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Decision-point-3 retrospective probe beginning, “That's the one I've turned over the most,” together with the subsequent no-competing-task and data-present counterfactual probes.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: Under concurrent non-handoff workload, the participant uses a familiar satisfactory response rather than fully evaluating accessible comparative evidence that could discriminate between a benign trend and an atypical rate of rise. This is a bounded, satisficing evidence-integration process: the historical comparison was feasible, relevant, and consciously deferred because the standard response felt sufficient in the moment.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The choice could partly reflect legitimate operational prioritization because the parameter was still within its normal band, lacked an alarm or technical-specification exceedance, and had an established checklist response. The interview nevertheless goes beyond ordinary triage: it establishes that the comparison was readily available, potentially decision-relevant, and likely would have affected the continue-versus-hold decision.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None required for the planned moderate-strength occurrence. The existing probes adequately establish accessibility, conscious deferral, competing-task load, and decision relevance without requiring an explicit bias label.

revision.location: Decision point 3, including the participant's explanation of the standard response and the two later counterfactual probes.
revision.current_defect: No material defect. The episode contains a distinct decision, accessible but unconsulted comparative evidence, a familiar satisfactory response, and a bounded-attention explanation.
preserve: The participant's distinction between a familiar response and a fuller comparison.
The finding that the rate of rise differed from earlier benign cases.
avoid_creating: Do not add a second separate instance of satisficing at the initial pump observation or pre-brief communication decision.
Do not state that the supervisor knowingly ignored a safety limit, because that would alter the intended moderate strength and occupational realism.
Do not imply that the eventual formal monitoring outcome itself proves the earlier reasoning was biased.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “The continue-and-monitor approach is what we've used for trends like this before, and it's worked, so that's the direction I went.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The familiar existing response was preferred over a potentially more disruptive hold-and-review option.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The preference for the existing checklist response is better explained by the targeted satisficing mechanism and by a reasonable reliance on established operating procedures. The text does not show a distinct aversion to changing course independent of incomplete evidence evaluation.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “[It] was already framed as a monitor-and-continue item in my head.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The prior framing may have reduced the amount of attention and communication devoted to potentially disconfirming trend information.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: There is no evidence that the participant selectively sought confirming information, discounted conflicting evidence after encountering it, or resisted the later historical comparison. Brief communication during an unrelated pre-brief is not sufficient to establish confirmation bias.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “There wasn't much to react to yet — within the band, no real trend history to speak of.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The early signal was treated as routine rather than as an immediately escalating abnormal condition.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The decision was supported by normal-band readings, absence of alarms, lack of trend history, logging, and increased monitoring. These are proportionate responses to ambiguous early equipment data rather than unjustified denial of risk.

nonbias_cues.cue: Management wanted the plant at the hold point for a grid commitment.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: This is an organizational and scheduling constraint. It does not by itself show that the supervisor distorted evidence, ignored a requirement, or selected an unsafe course.

nonbias_cues.cue: The supervisor increased monitoring rather than immediately calling the system engineer at the first pump indication.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: The parameter remained in band, no alarm had occurred, and the participant lacked meaningful trend history. The response included active monitoring and an escalation condition rather than dismissal.

nonbias_cues.cue: The supervisor sought a reactor engineer's view on the steam-generator level blip.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Seeking corroboration for a control-system explanation is calibrated expertise and risk management, not indecision, authority bias, or reliance on automation.

nonbias_cues.cue: Automatic control corrected the steam-generator level blip.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Reliance on automatic control would require evidence of uncritical deference despite contrary indications. Here, the participant still consulted the reactor engineer.

nonbias_cues.cue: The pump later entered formal close monitoring.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: A later adverse or more serious outcome does not retrospectively establish that the prior decision process was biased. It supplies context for examining the missed comparative evidence, not proof by outcome.

nonbias_cues.cue: The participant states in hindsight that the rate of rise differed from earlier cases.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: This is retrospective knowledge. It becomes relevant only because the interview separately establishes that the comparative data was accessible at the time and could have been consulted.

causal_claims.claim: Concurrent preparation for the surveillance pre-brief and the ascension schedule narrowed the supervisor's evidence search and contributed to deferring the historical vibration comparison.
causal_claims.textual_support: “Having one clear task instead of two changes what feels worth doing in the moment versus what can wait.”
causal_claims.assessment: Moderately supported by the participant's contemporaneous reconstruction and the absence of a turnover obligation, but it remains a self-reported causal account rather than independently verified causal evidence.

causal_claims.claim: If the historical comparison had been consulted at the upper-third threshold, it could have shifted the supervisor toward holding rather than continuing.
causal_claims.textual_support: “If it had shown the rate of rise was outside what we'd seen before, I'd have leaned toward holding rather than continuing.”
causal_claims.assessment: A plausible conditional causal claim. It appropriately remains probabilistic (“possibly” and “would have leaned”) and does not overstate certainty.

causal_claims.claim: The later formal close-monitoring action establishes that continuing earlier was cognitively biased.
causal_claims.textual_support: The interview does not expressly make this claim.
causal_claims.assessment: Not supported and should not be inferred. The later outcome cannot alone validate the bias classification.

correlation_causation_risks: The pre-brief deadline and ascension schedule co-occur at decision point 3, so the interview cannot isolate the independent contribution of each source of pressure.
The conclusion that the historical comparison would have changed the decision is a retrospective counterfactual and may be affected by outcome knowledge.
The later technical-specification close-monitoring action is temporally downstream but does not prove that an earlier hold was required or that the earlier monitoring decision was unreasonable.
causal_audit.changed_variable: Presence of an imminent shift-turnover handoff obligation at decision point 3. The interview replaces that obligation with a time-boxed, unrelated surveillance-test pre-brief due in approximately 45 minutes.
held_constant: Feedwater pump 1B vibration trend magnitude and timing.
Steam-generator level event and its resolution.
Availability of the on-call reactor engineer.
Accessibility of historical vibration data on the plant computer.
Availability of continue, hold, review, and monitoring alternatives.
The intended decision point and moderate-strength satisficing mechanism.
causal_audit.explanation: The interview credibly implements the changed variable: it expressly excludes an imminent turnover, identifies the unrelated pre-brief as the competing deadline, and repeatedly confirms that no handoff forced the deferral. The causal substitution is coherent because the new task supplies comparable attentional competition without changing the equipment signal or available evidence. Fidelity is moderate rather than strong because equivalence in the magnitude and character of turnover versus pre-brief workload is asserted narratively but cannot be independently established from this single interview.

global_revision_constraints: Do not treat the later formal close-monitoring outcome as proof of bias.
Maintain the distinction between ordinary early-stage monitoring at decision point 1 and satisficing at decision point 3.
Maintain the absence of an imminent turnover handoff while retaining the unrelated pre-brief deadline as the counterfactual competing task.
Do not add a second independently countable familiar-heuristic or deferred-evidence episode.
